mechanism_narrative: Workplace mobility has been recovering from -17.4 toward -16.3/-16.7 over three weeks, indicating gradual return of commuting and lunchtime/after-work routines that generate incidental retail trips. This sustained workplace recovery should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as foot traffic near offices increases.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -17.4 to -16.3 over t-3w to t-2w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is not higher than its last-28-day mean despite WORKPLACES continuing to trend upward, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC rose for three consecutive weeks (-24.6 to -18.1) before reversing to -19.9 in the latest week. This single-week reversal after sustained momentum signals behavioral fatigue or saturation in discretionary outings, predicting a short-term continued decline in RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks before any potential rebound.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC falls more than 1.0 point week-on-week immediately after three consecutive weeks of increase
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC moved -24.6,-20.7,-18.1,-19.9 showing a reversal in week t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's mean over the following week(s) immediately rebounds above the t-1w level rather than continuing to decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility jointly determine commuter-driven retail exposure. When both series improve together (less negative), combined commuter flows through transit hubs and office districts amplify retail footfall beyond what either series would predict alone, raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve (become less negative) in the same week relative to the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -25.6 to -22.0 over three weeks while WORKPLACES improved from -17.4 to -16.3
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next two weeks despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES jointly improving, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Following the end of Spain's state of alarm in May 2021, successive weeks of improving TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility reflect policy-driven relaxation of restrictions on movement. If this relaxation regime persists for three or more consecutive weeks, RETAIL_REC should rise over the following four weeks as capacity limits on retail and hospitality venues continue to ease.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both show sustained improvement for three or more consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both series show multi-week improvement trends through t-1w
failure_condition: If new restrictions are reinstated or RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite continued TRANSIT/WORKPLACES improvement, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: As Madrid approaches peak summer heat in late June, outdoor park visitation is expected to decline from its recent high of 12.9 toward lower levels seen at t-0w (9.3), with displaced leisure activity substituting toward indoor retail and grocery/pharmacy venues, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines for a second consecutive week while GROCERY_PHARM remains positive
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from 12.9 to 9.3 in the latest week
failure_condition: If PARKS continues to decline but RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

Once RESIDENTIAL falls below a threshold near 3.0, this reduced home-bound behavior is expected to translate into more frequent out-of-home retail visits over the following two weeks.

evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined monotonically from 5.0 to 3.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL drops below 3.0 but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Emerging variant-driven public health concerns around mid-2021 could prompt renewed caution even without formal restrictions. If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both simultaneously stall or reverse for two consecutive weeks, this signals a behavioral or policy-driven pullback that should suppress RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.

failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's mean over the next week is not lower than the t-0w level, the seasonal outmigration hypothesis is rejected.
